name: HeliBoard
hook: The keyboard logs every word you type — HeliBoard is 100% offline with zero internet permission, so it physically cannot phone home.
bullets: Declares no internet permission — Android itself blocks it from ever phoning home
On-device suggestions, spell check, and multilingual dictionaries
Material You theming from your wallpaper, plus custom colors and backgrounds
Clipboard history, one-handed and split layouts, number pad, backup/restore
benefits: Nothing you type ever leaves the phone — there is no code path to a server
Predictions without a company quietly building a profile of your vocabulary
Looks native on Android 12+ by pulling colors straight from your wallpaper
Small, auditable code base built on the stock Android keyboard
setupSteps: Install HeliBoard from F-Droid or the project's GitHub releases
Enable it in Android Settings → System → On-screen keyboard
Pick your languages and import dictionaries for suggestions
Optionally supply a swipe library for glide typing, then match the theme to your wallpaper
details: HeliBoard is a free, open-source Android keyboard based on the AOSP keyboard (via OpenBoard), and its headline feature sits right in its manifest: the app declares no internet permission, so Android itself guarantees it can never transmit your typing — suggestions, spell check, and dictionaries all run on-device. You get the familiar stock-keyboard experience plus multilingual typing, fully customizable layouts and symbol/numpad arrangements, clipboard history, one-handed and split modes, and backup/restore of settings and learned words. Theming follows Material You dynamic colors from your wallpaper on Android 12+, respects day/night, or can be set to custom colors and background images. One honest caveat the project itself flags: glide (swipe) typing depends on a closed-source gesture library — the same kind Gboard ships — that cannot be bundled with the app, so you optionally supply it from a GApps package if you want swipe. Everything else works with zero network access.
